title: Terraform-driven stability gatekeeper for plan-led zero-downtime data-plane switchover
creator: Anika Shah
body:
Overview:

We need a robust, plan-first automation that performs private (VPC) runtime/data-plane upgrades with zero customer-facing downtime and safe automated rollback. Current rollout controllers rely on ad-hoc canaries and manual terraform interventions. This ticket proposes a Terraform-driven "stability gatekeeper" that: (1) computes a canonical terraform plan diff for an upgrade, (2) orchestrates staged tenant slices using a plan-derived execution graph, (3) uses passive probes and mirrored synthetic traffic for health gating (no full cutover canary), and (4) automatically triggers fast rollback using saved state snapshots if stability criteria are violated.

Goals / Non-goals:
- Goal: Deploy runtime/data-plane changes (runtime binary, kernel flags, network policy, instance type/AMI) across VPC deployments without customer-visible errors and with automated rollback when safety gates fail.
- Goal: Use terraform plan as source-of-truth to generate safe execution steps (diff-aware).
- Non-goal: Replace the existing blue/green operator today — this is a complementary safer path for complex stateful upgrades where live probe evidence is required.

Acceptance criteria:
- The gatekeeper can ingest a terraform plan JSON and produce an execution plan that lists ordered tenant slices and per-slice terraform apply commands.
- Health gating rules evaluate passive metrics (mirrored request error-rate, tail latency, streaming SSE errors) and cached-KV warmup indicators; gates can be configured per-tenant slice.
- If a gate violates (eg. error-rate > 0.5% sustained 60s or 99p latency increase > 40%), the system executes an automated rollback using the stored terraform state snapshot and fences traffic to the failing slice within 2 minutes.
- No customer-facing RPC errors above baseline for >99.9% of requests across an upgrade rollout (measured in internal canary traffic and mirror-derived metrics).
- End-to-end e2e test harness reproduces a typical runtime upgrade with induced faults and validates rollback path.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Terraform planner adapter:
   - Add a small service that runs `terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan` and `terraform show -json` to produce a machine-readable graph.
   - Extract resource groupings and tenant attachments (map to our slice concept).
   - Tag plan nodes with metadata (type: instance/replacement/stateful-vol, risk: high/medium/low) using heuristics.
2) Plan-to-graph transform:
   - Convert plan into an ordered execution graph allowing parallelization where safe (stateless nodes first, then stateful with preflight).
   - Persist a signed plan snapshot (immutable) to the upgrade artifact store for audit & rollback.
3) Passive probe harness:
   - Create passive-mirroring pipeline: mirror 5-10% of production traffic to upgraded slices (no activation). Mirror responses compared against baseline (error, latency, semantic checks).
   - Synthetic lightweight traffic generator (non-invasive) that exercises common code-paths (small prompt generation + long-seq).
4) Stability gate engine:
   - Evaluate sliding windows of metrics and decide PASS / SOFT-Fail / HARD-Fail per slice.
   - Provide configurable thresholds per release type (hotfix vs major).
5) Automated rollback operator:
   - On HARD-Fail, mark slice fenced, run terraform apply against the saved pre-upgrade state snapshot (or revert resource replacements), and re-route traffic back to last-known-good nodes.
   - Emit incident with root-cause hints (resource diff, metric spike).
6) Observability + runbook:
   - Dashboard showing plan diff, per-slice progress, gating decisions, and time-to-rollback.
   - Pre-populated runbook play for on-call with quick actions (approve-continue, force-rollback, pause-rollout).

Rollout steps (operator flow):
- PREPARE: Author upgrade branch, create terraform plan JSON. Gatekeeper validates plan (schema, risk tags).
- PREVERIFY: Run `terraform apply` in a dry-run harness that creates ephemeral replicas in a sandbox VPC to sanity-check resource creation.
- SNAPSHOT: Persist current terraform state and mark snapshot id.
- PATCH SLICE: Apply plan steps for slice N to create new instances / replace images.
- MIRROR & MONITOR: Start passive mirror and synthetic probes for slice N for a configurable observation window (default 3m).
- EVALUATE: Gate engine applies rules; if PASS, continue to next slice. If SOFT-Fail, pause and extend observation; if HARD-Fail, trigger rollback.
- ROLLBACK: Fence slice (no live traffic), apply snapshot state to restore resources, confirm baseline metrics, proceed to investigation.

Key health signals (examples):
- mirrored_error_rate (5s/60s windows), mirrored_99p_latency, replica_kv_hit_rate (percent of warmed keys), grpc_stream_resets, streaming-token-drop-rate, infra_cpu_steal
- plan_diff_tags: node_replaced_stateful=true increases gating stringency

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for plan parser and graph transform.
- Integration tests using local terraform with mocked AWS/GCP resources (terraform local backend) to verify plan snapshots and rollback applies.
- Chaos scenarios using the staging cluster: network partitions, injected high latency on KV layer, transient OOM in an upgraded binary. Validate automatic rollback and audit trail.
- Runbook-driven tabletop exercise with SRE/PM/SE to exercise aborts, forced-rollbacks.

Telemetry & Cost controls:
- Emit events per plan id: plan_created, slice_applied, probe_started, gate_result, rollback_initiated, rollback_complete. Events linkable to trace ids.
- Sampling rule for mirrored traffic to limit egress and cost (default 5%).

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Terraform state rollback approach: restore-from-snapshot vs apply inverse plan. Restore is faster but may miss implicit drift; inverse apply is safer but complex for replacements. Recommendation: use restore snapshot for initial MVP and experiment with inverse-plan in parallel.
- How aggressive should mirror sampling be for high-traffic customers vs small tenants? We need per-customer configs.
- Interaction with Dedicated customers where we can't launch ephemeral replicas — require a constrained path and operator approval.

Backwards compatibility / migration notes:
- Existing blue/green can be left intact; new gatekeeper is opt-in via a `plan_mode=stability_gate` flag in the deployment pipeline.
- Provide a compatibility shim to generate plan snapshots from older `stateful-update` flows.

Security / compliance:
- Plan snapshots are signed and stored in an encrypted bucket. Access controls by IAM role.
- All rollback operations audited and gated by RBAC; emergency rollback requires on-call approval unless configured for auto-rollback.

Links & artifacts:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Plan-Driven+Stability+Gatekeeper

- Spike PR (planner adapter): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4821
- Observability dashboard draft: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/upgrade-gate/plan-gate-overview

Operational runbook snippet (short):
- If gate HARD-Fails: mark incident, rollback via operator UI -> confirm rollback initiated -> monitor mirrored metrics to confirm baseline restored -> rotate investigation tickets to runtime team.
- If gate SOFT-Fails: pause rollout, extend observation window to 10m, optionally run additional synthetic probes targeted to suspected code-paths.
